name: call-frequency-max-a-window-it-can-only-see-part-of-is-left-unjudged
why: A CAP WHOSE LIMIT THE WINDOW ITSELF DECIDES IS NOT THE HARMLESS DIRECTION, AND OWNER DECISION L NEVER SAID IT WAS. The decision lets a cap evaluate a partial window because a short count cannot exceed an authored number. This limit is not authored: it is floor(availableDays / n), so a partial window shrinks the allowance alongside the count and false-positives exactly as a floor does. Four of the five windows here reach outside the evaluable range and are reported rather than judged — the first of them would otherwise show one call against an allowance of zero — and the one whole window carries the real violation.

expected.explanation: 2 calls in the 3 days from 2026-08-01 to 2026-08-03; at most 1 is permitted. The person was available on 3 days of that window and the rule allows one call in every 2: leave, days before the join date and days off the roster are not counted, so the allowance falls around them rather than rising.

skipped.reason: The window 2026-07-30 to 2026-08-01 is not wholly inside the evaluable range 2026-08-01 to 2026-08-03, so part of it could not be counted. A count that is short cannot exceed an authored cap, but it can fall below a floor, miss a target, or shrink a limit the window's own contents decide — so this window was left unjudged.
